quests.hint: A job posting seeks someone who 'thinks like a founder,' spots new opportunities, and isn't afraid to take risks starting new projects.
quests.explanation: -AL turns ENTREPRENEUR into the adjective ENTREPRENEURIAL, relating to the mindset or activity of starting and running new business ventures.
quests.instruction: Which suffix turns this noun into an adjective?

quests.hint: A manager who takes full responsibility when a project fails, instead of blaming the team.
quests.explanation: ACCOUNTABILITY stacks -ABLE (capable of being called to account) and -ITY (the quality of that) onto ACCOUNT, meaning the obligation to accept responsibility for one's actions.
quests.meaningBreakdown: ACCOUNT (root) + ABIL (suffix, 'capable of being') + ITY (suffix, forms a noun of quality)
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A design team where every member contributes ideas together, rather than one person working alone and assigning tasks.
quests.explanation: -IVE forms COLLABORATIVE from COLLABORATE, characterized by people working together. -MENT would instead build a noun, COLLABORATION, the act itself, not an adjective describing the style of work.
quests.instruction: Which suffix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: EXTRA- means 'outside, beyond.' Which word describes the debate club and soccer team, activities students do outside their regular class schedule?
quests.explanation: EXTRA- + CURRICULAR = EXTRACURRICULAR, outside the normal curriculum or coursework.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: A university course that combines biology, computer science, and ethics all in a single semester-long project.
quests.explanation: INTERDISCIPLINARY combines INTER- ('between') with DISCIPLINE and -ARY, drawing on and connecting multiple academic fields at once.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A first-year college student who hasn't yet earned their bachelor's degree.
quests.explanation: UNDER- + GRADUATE = UNDERGRADUATE, a student below the graduate level, still working toward their first degree. POST- would instead describe someone already past that stage, studying for an advanced degree.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: MULTI- means 'many.' Which word describes a printer that can also scan, fax, and copy documents, all in one machine?
quests.explanation: MULTI- + FUNCTIONAL = MULTIFUNCTIONAL, capable of performing many different functions.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: A hospital's new software can share patient records seamlessly with every other clinic's system in the state, regardless of brand.
quests.explanation: INTEROPERABLE combines INTER- ('between') with OPERATE and -ABLE, capable of working together with other systems.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A company closes its single headquarters and instead lets regional offices around the world make their own decisions independently.
quests.explanation: DECENTRALIZATION combines DE- ('away from') with CENTRAL, -IZE ('to make'), and -ATION (forms a noun), the process of spreading control away from one central authority. CO- would instead suggest bringing things together, the opposite direction.
quests.meaningBreakdown: DE (prefix, 'away from') + CENTRAL (root) + IZ (suffix, 'to make') + ATION (suffix, forms a noun)
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A city council that posts every budget decision online for residents to review, with nothing hidden.
quests.explanation: -CY, a close relative of -ITY and -ACY, turns TRANSPARENT into TRANSPARENCY, the quality of being open and easy to see through, literally or figuratively.
quests.meaningBreakdown: TRANSPAREN (root) + CY (suffix, forms a noun of quality)
quests.instruction: Which suffix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: An elected official who answers tough questions honestly at a town hall instead of dodging them.
quests.explanation: ACCOUNTABLE is ACCOUNT + -ABLE, capable of being called to explain one's actions — the adjective at the root of ACCOUNTABILITY from earlier.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A local police department has legal authority to make arrests only within the boundaries of its own city.
quests.explanation: JURISDICTION combines JURIS- ('law') with DICT ('say' — the same root from PREDICT and BENEDICTION) and -ION, literally the area where the law 'speaks,' or has authority.
quests.meaningBreakdown: JURIS (root, 'law') + DICT (root, 'say') + ION (suffix, forms a noun)
quests.instruction: Which suffix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: BIO- means 'life.' Which suffix completes a word describing a plastic bag replacement that natural bacteria can fully break down in just a few months?
quests.explanation: BIO- ('life, living things') + DEGRADE + -ABLE = BIODEGRADABLE, capable of being broken down naturally by living organisms.
quests.instruction: Which suffix completes this word?

quests.hint: A material like uranium that constantly emits energy and particles, requiring careful handling and storage.
quests.explanation: RADIOACTIVE combines RADIO- ('rays, radiation') with ACTIVE, describing a substance that actively emits radiation.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: The process a leaf uses to convert sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into the energy a plant needs to grow.
quests.explanation: PHOTO- ('light') + SYNTHESIS ('putting together') = PHOTOSYNTHESIS, literally 'putting together using light,' the process plants use to make food from sunlight. BIO- would instead just mean 'life' in general, without specifying that light is the energy source.
quests.instruction: Which root correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A tabloid takes a routine celebrity divorce and turns it into a dramatic front-page scandal with exaggerated headlines.
quests.explanation: -IZE turns the adjective SENSATIONAL into the verb SENSATIONALIZE, to present something in a deliberately exaggerated, shocking way to attract attention.
quests.instruction: Which suffix turns this adjective into a verb?

quests.hint: A news anchor who's supposed to just report the facts starts adding personal opinions and emotional commentary instead.
quests.explanation: EDITORIALIZE is EDITORIAL + -IZE, to express personal opinions while presenting something that should be neutral, like news.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A new law that half the public strongly supports and the other half strongly opposes, sparking heated debate on both sides.
quests.explanation: CONTRO- (a form of 'against') + VERSE (from VERT, 'turn') + -IAL = CONTROVERSIAL, causing strong disagreement because opinions turn against each other. This connects back to the whole VERT/VERSE family: INTROVERT, EXTROVERT, CONVERT, DIVERT, and now CONTROVERSIAL.
quests.meaningBreakdown: CONTRO (root, 'against') + VERSE (root, 'turn') + IAL (suffix, forms an adjective)
quests.instruction: Which suffix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A decision so final that once it's made, it legally can never be undone or called back, no matter what.
quests.explanation: IR- ('not') + REVOKE ('call back') + -ABLE = IRREVOCABLE, incapable of being revoked or reversed. This connects directly back to REVOKE, the 'call back' root from Phase 7.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IR (prefix, 'not') + REVOKE (root, 'call back') + ABLE (suffix, 'capable of being')
quests.instruction: Which suffix completes this three-part word?

quests.hint: A used car's sticker price that the salesman hints could come down if you're willing to talk numbers.
quests.explanation: NEGOTIABLE is NEGOTIATE + -ABLE, capable of being discussed and adjusted through bargaining.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: Lawyers argue in court over whether a brand-new state law actually follows the rules laid out in the country's founding legal document.
quests.explanation: CONSTITUTIONALITY stacks -AL (noun → adjective) and -ITY (forms a noun of quality) onto CONSTITUTION, meaning whether or not something aligns with a nation's constitution. -NESS wouldn't complete this chain — the word specifically ends in -ALITY, following the same pattern as PRODUCTIVITY and CREATIVITY.
quests.meaningBreakdown: CONSTITUTION (root) + AL (suffix, noun → adjective) + ITY (suffix, forms a noun of quality)
quests.instruction: Which suffix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: Instead of waiting to be told what to do, a new employee identifies a problem and starts solving it on her own.
quests.explanation: -IVE turns INITIATE into INITIATIVE, the ability or action of starting something independently, without being prompted.
quests.instruction: Which suffix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: An official review confirms that a university's nursing program meets national standards before students can enroll and earn a recognized degree.
quests.explanation: ACCREDITATION combines AC- (a form of AD-, 'toward') with CREDIT ('trust, belief') and -ATION, the formal process of officially recognizing that an institution meets certain standards.
quests.meaningBreakdown: AC (prefix, 'toward') + CREDIT (root, 'trust') + ATION (suffix, forms a noun)
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A firefighter runs into a burning building without hesitation to save a family — the kind of bravery most people will never show.
quests.explanation: EXTRA- + ORDINARY = EXTRAORDINARY, going far beyond what is usual or expected. NON- would instead just mean 'not ordinary' in a flat, neutral sense, missing the sense of remarkable achievement EXTRA- carries here.
quests.instruction: Which prefix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: A single corporation with offices, factories, and employees spread across dozens of different countries.
quests.explanation: MULTI- + NATIONAL = MULTINATIONAL, operating across many nations. This reviews MULTI- alongside INTERNATIONAL, between nations, from earlier — a subtle but real difference in scale and structure.
quests.instruction: Which prefix fits this situation?

quests.hint: A journalist tracks down three independent witnesses and official documents before publishing a claim, to back it up with solid proof.
quests.explanation: SUBSTANTIATE is built from SUBSTANTIAL ('solid, having substance') plus -ATE, to provide solid evidence supporting a claim.
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: The branch of government specifically responsible for writing and voting on new laws, separate from the courts or the president.
quests.explanation: -IVE forms LEGISLATIVE from LEGISLATE, relating to the making of laws. -TION would instead build LEGISLATION, the laws themselves — a noun, not an adjective describing a branch of government.
quests.instruction: Which suffix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: Some people claim to have a 'sixth sense' — the supposed ability to perceive things beyond sight, sound, touch, taste, and smell.
quests.explanation: EXTRA- + SENSORY = EXTRASENSORY, beyond the normal five senses. This checkpoint reviews EXTRA- and MULTI-, two prefixes meaning 'beyond' and 'many' that both appear constantly in professional and academic writing.
quests.instruction: Checkpoint: which prefix means 'beyond the usual'?

quests.hint: The legal right to keep your medical records, financial details, and personal messages away from public view.
quests.explanation: -CY forms PRIVACY from PRIVATE, the state of being free from public attention or interference. This checkpoint reviews the -CY/-ITY/-ACY family of quality-noun suffixes you've now seen across TRANSPARENCY, ACCURACY, and PRIVACY.
quests.meaningBreakdown: PRIVA (root) + CY (suffix, forms a noun of quality)
quests.instruction: Checkpoint: which suffix forms a noun of quality here?

quests.hint: Two countries whose economies rely so heavily on each other's trade that a crisis in one immediately affects the other.
quests.explanation: INTER- ('between') + DEPEND ('rely on') + -ENT = INTERDEPENDENT, relying on each other mutually. After nearly 190 levels, breaking apart a formal, professional-sounding word like this should feel like second nature — the same skill used on REDO back in Level 1.
quests.meaningBreakdown: INTER (prefix, 'between/mutually') + DEPEND (root, 'rely on') + ENT (suffix, forms an adjective)
quests.instruction: Checkpoint: which prefix means 'between, mutually'?
